title: 4 Movies Left In 2026 (And Beyond) That Are About To Wreck Us Emotionally
dek: Witchy sisters, a mask-wearing detective duo, Doctor Doom himself, and one very delayed Bat-sequel — here's everything we're still counting down to.

items.heading: Sally And Gillian Owens Are FINALLY Coming Home
items.text: Nearly three decades after the original spellbound us, Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman are reuniting as the Owens sisters, and the trailer already has us reaching for tissues and moonlight-appropriate outfits. The sequel pulls from Alice Hoffman's own follow-up novel, with Sally and Gillian facing down the family curse all over again — this time with Joey King along for the ride.

images.caption: Sandra Bullock returns as Sally Owens
Nicole Kidman returns as Gillian Owens

items.heading: Judy And Nick Are Back On The Case — And This Time There's A Snake Involved
items.text: Ginnifer Goodwin and Jason Bateman are slipping back into their badges as Judy Hopps and Nick Wilde, and this go-round the ZPD's favorite mismatched duo gets ordered into couples counseling before chasing down a mysterious reptile who turns Zootopia upside down. Ke Huy Quan joins the cast as the venomous-but-maybe-not-so-bad Gary De'Snake, and the trailer promises brand new corners of the city we've never seen.

images.caption: Ginnifer Goodwin voices Judy Hopps again
Jason Bateman is back as Nick Wilde

items.heading: Doctor Doom Has Entered The Chat And The MCU Will Never Be The Same
items.text: Robert Downey Jr. is officially back in the MCU — not as Tony Stark, but as the terrifying Victor Von Doom — and the trailer makes clear the Fantastic Four already have a complicated history with him. The Russo brothers are stacking basically every corner of the franchise into one movie, from the Thunderbolts to Fox's original X-Men cast, making this one of the biggest ensemble team-ups Marvel has ever attempted.

images.caption: Robert Downey Jr. returns as Doctor Doom

items.heading: Yes, It Got Delayed AGAIN — But The First Look At Pattinson's Return Still Broke The Internet
items.text: Look, we're not going to pretend The Batman Part II hasn't bounced around the release calendar — it's now landing February 18, 2028 instead of its once-planned 2026 date, giving director Matt Reeves extra time in post. But Robert Pattinson's already teased that the script is "extraordinary," and the first camera-test footage of him back in the cowl, plus new additions like Scarlett Johansson and Sebastian Stan, has fans convinced the wait will be worth it.

images.caption: The Batman Part II is now set for February 18, 2028
Robert Pattinson suits back up as the Dark Knight
Scarlett Johansson joins the sequel's cast
